title: simulacr
text: simulacr implements outbreak simulation using contact-driven branching processes. main features package include: simulate_outbreak(): main function, simulating epidemic spread using inputs generation time distribution, individual transmission rates, contact matrices; outputs simulacr object, list containing linelist transmission tree, can converted epicontacts objects visualisation, plotted using plot(...) simulate_outbreak_step(): step-wise version simulator, designed calling packages make_pmf_delay(): generate probability mass functions delays distributions make_disc_gamma(): build discretised Gamma distributions delay distributions make_panmictic_contacts(): generate contact matrix assuming random mixing draw_labels(): wrapper function generate random alphanumeric labels

title: simulacr
text: brief example illustrates can simulate outbreak.   Note: interactive version plot, check simulacr website.
code: ## make a generation time distribution gen_time <- make_pmf_delay(make_disc_gamma(10, 7)) plot(   gen_time(0:30), type = "h", lend = 2, lwd = 10,    main = "Generation time distribution",    xlab = "Delay from primary to secondary infection (days)",    ylab = "p(delay)" ) ## simulate an outbreak using random mixing  ## (no contacts matrix provided -> all individuals are in contact by default) set.seed(1) res <- simulate_outbreak(   n = 100, # 100 individuals in the population   duration = 365, # simulate for a year   w = gen_time, # generation time distribution   tau = runif(100, 0.01, 0.05) # individual transmission rates, from 0.01 to 0.05 )  names(res) #> [1] "linelist" "tree" res #> $linelist #> # A tibble: 100 × 3 #>    id     casedef date_infection #>    <chr>  <chr>            <dbl> #>  1 eLGzdD case                 1 #>  2 8Tvbyj case                44 #>  3 MQ90i6 case                45 #>  4 RdzUUA case                43 #>  5 kSVCEa case                30 #>  6 Z42dvb case                46 #>  7 YWzVgb case                40 #>  8 EGjSAk case                51 #>  9 6rcYKS case                34 #> 10 VBW4HD case                33 #> # ℹ 90 more rows #>  #> $tree #> # A tibble: 91 × 3 #>    from   to      date #>    <chr>  <chr>  <dbl> #>  1 <NA>   eLGzdD     1 #>  2 eLGzdD LjuhEd    14 #>  3 LjuhEd HmhA3k    18 #>  4 LjuhEd J98DE8    23 #>  5 HmhA3k Lwe2aP    23 #>  6 LjuhEd MOZ5Ca    23 #>  7 HmhA3k yKVg67    25 #>  8 J98DE8 knhTUJ    25 #>  9 MOZ5Ca 3eZzb4    25 #> 10 HmhA3k UwrMJp    26 #> # ℹ 81 more rows #>  #> attr(,"class") #> [1] "simulacr" "list" plot(res)

what: Simulate outbreaks with transmission trees — simulate_outbreak
title: Simulate outbreaks with transmission trees — simulate_outbreak
text: function implements contact-driven branching process outbreak simulator. Outbreaks start single infection otherwise fully susceptible population size non first time step. New cases generated time step infectious individuals, forces infection depending generation time distribution, individual transmission rates, contacts individuals. function returns linelist including non-cases cases, well transmission tree listing transmission events shape data.frame columns , , date. function user-facing; use simulacr engine another package, may want use low-level function [simulate_outbreak_step()].

title: Simulate outbreaks with transmission trees — simulate_outbreak
code: simulate_outbreak(   n,   duration = 1L,   w = c(0, 1),   tau = 0,   contacts = NULL,   label_size = 6 )

title: Simulate outbreaks with transmission trees — simulate_outbreak
text: n integer indicating number individuals population; default. duration integer indicating number time steps run simulation ; defaults 1L (.e. initial infection generated). w probability mass function generation time distribution, produced [make_pmf_delay()], specified numeric vector, function, distcrete object. Defaults point mass 1 (.e. secondary infections take place exactly 1 time step primary infection). tau numeric vector length n containing individual transmission rates; single value recycled; defaults 0 (transmission). contacts Contacts individuals population. can specified two ways: ) n x n matrix entries correspond contact presence intensities, ii) function single argument t (time step) generating matrix time step. NULL (default), assume random-mixing population, .e. individuals contact every time step. label_size integer indicating length labels generated [draw_labels()], used unique individual identifiers. Defaults 6.

title: Simulate outbreaks with transmission trees — simulate_outbreak
text: force infection (FOI) individual \(\) \(j\) time \(t\) defined : \(\lambda_{t, \rightarrow j} = I_{t,} C_{t, \rightarrow j} \tau_{t,} w(t - T_i)\) total FOI experienced individual  time  summed possible sources infection: \(\lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j} = S_{t,j} \sum_i \lambda_{t, \rightarrow j} \) follows individual \(j\) becomes infected time \(t+1\) according Bernoulli distribution probability: \( 1 - e^{-\lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j}} \) keep track chains transmission, infector \(j\), denoted \(alpha_j\), drawn Multinomial distribution weighted respective FOIs directed towards \(j\): \( \alpha_j \sim \mathcal{M}(1, \lambda_{t, 1 \rightarrow j} / \lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j} ,\lambda_{t, 2 \rightarrow j} / \lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j} , \ldots , \lambda_{t, N \rightarrow j} / \lambda_{t, \bullet \rightarrow j}  ) \)
